chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Big tips at the Vendome during the Depression
summary: The Vendome paid $35 a week plus tips; the quintet never took home under $50 each a night and blew it on pool.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I imagine about nineteen, yeah, about eighteen or nineteen. About nineteen, nineteen or twenty, I guess. And then -- well, let's see, this was 19 -- I think this was 1930, this was around August of 1930, and I went into the Vendome, and this was something else. This was $35.00 a week, and it was like Harlem, you know. All the white people would come down, you know, and people in different rackets and things, and they liked you, and they would give you big tips, and it was the depression time, and we never walked in -- and I went back, so this made five of us, four rhythm and a trumpet.
And we used to pick the tips up every night. The girls would go around and make tips, they'd give us half, and then people would come in and ask for different numbers and give you money.
We had some guy come in there, he'd give you a fifty dollar bill. And so we split up -- I don't remember a night walking out of there with under $50.00.
Uh-huh, under $50.00, and you blew it. You blew it.
You were going to get it again tomorrow night, so why not?
